def: A search method that keeps a population of candidates and repeatedly selects the fitter ones and varies them to make the next generation.
The data structure that encodes one candidate solution in an evolutionary algorithm, such as a bit string, a vector or a program.
The score that an evolutionary algorithm tries to increase, computed by evaluating a candidate.
An evolutionary algorithm over fixed-length strings, using selection, crossover and mutation.
Choosing a parent by drawing k individuals at random and taking the fittest of them.
How strongly an evolutionary algorithm favours the fittest individuals when choosing parents.
A population settling on a mediocre solution because it lost its diversity before finding better regions.
Copying the best few individuals unchanged into the next generation so the best score never falls.
Building a child genome from parts of two parent genomes.
An evolutionary method for real-valued vectors that relies on Gaussian mutation with an adapted step size.
Rechenberg's rule to grow the mutation step size when more than a fifth of mutations improve the parent, and shrink it otherwise.
The idea that good solutions are assembled from short high-quality fragments that crossover can combine.
